metaDescription: Six concrete and concrete-look coffee tables compared on real cement, MgO or fiberglass, weight, indoor and outdoor use, shape and sealing before you buy.
expertTake: The Modway Brion round table is our top pick because its listing describes a concrete tapered cylinder that works indoors or on a patio. The FESTIVITY 28 in MgO drum is the value pick for a small room. Skip the category if you expect a heavy poured slab, because most tables here are lightweight concrete, MgO board or fiberglass made to look like concrete, and the weight differs by tens of pounds.
introParagraphs: Concrete tables bring a cool, matte, architectural look to a living room and pair well with wood, leather and linen. Real poured concrete is very heavy, and standard concrete furniture often weighs 80 to 150 lb, with fiber-reinforced types noticeably lighter. Many tables sold as concrete are lightweight blends, MgO board or fiberglass with a concrete finish, and the difference affects weight, repair and how the surface wears.

We evaluated each table from its published specifications and patterns in owner feedback, not from handling it. Listings use the word concrete for several materials, so we state what each one says it is made of. The lineup spans round drums, a pedestal table, a legged table and an oval so you can match the shape to your room.

products.name: Modway Brion 34 in Round Concrete Coffee Table, Tapered Cylinder, Indoor or Outdoor
products.description:
The Modway Brion is a 34 in round tapered cylinder coffee table that the listing describes as concrete with a smooth, polished finish, suitable for indoor or outdoor use. The listing calls it a low center table for the living room or the patio. It is the cleanest concrete statement in the lineup and the only one that leads with a tapered drum shape.

The tradeoff is weight and pores. A 34 in concrete drum is heavy and hard to move, and concrete is porous, so unsealed surfaces can stain from oil, wine or coffee unless a sealer is applied. The listing does not give a weight in the text we reviewed, so check the page before planning to move it up stairs. Compared with the lightweight tables, it is a more solid object but less forgiving on a hard floor.

Place a felt or rubber pad under the base to protect floors, and use coasters. Wipe spills quickly and reseal the surface if it darkens. It suits a modern living room or a covered patio where one heavy, quiet, sculptural table is wanted.
products.bestFor: Modern living rooms and covered patios that want a solid concrete drum.

Smooth polished surface wipes clean when it is sealed
Works indoors or on a patio, so it can move with the seasons
34 in diameter suits a sectional or two chairs and a sofa
cons: Heavy, and the listing text gives no weight, so moving it needs planning
Porous concrete can stain from oil, wine or coffee unless sealed

products.name: FESTIVITY 28 in Round MgO Coffee Table, Concrete Drum-Look Finish, Indoor and Outdoor

specList.label: Finish
specList.value: Concrete drum look with porous texture

products.description:
The FESTIVITY is a 28 in round drum coffee table made of high-density MgO, magnesium oxide board, with a concrete-look finish and a finely textured, porous surface. The listing says MgO offers excellent water resistance and a strong load-bearing structure. It is the smallest and lightest table in the lineup and the only one that is clear about being MgO.

The tradeoff is that MgO is a board, not poured concrete, so it can chip at edges and rim and does not have the weight of real concrete. A porous textured surface can hold stains and dust, and a 28 in drum is small for a large seating group. Compared with the Modway, it is lighter and cheaper but less solid in feel.

Seal the surface if you use it outdoors and add a felt pad underneath. Wipe it with a damp cloth. It suits a small living room, a balcony or a corner between two chairs.
products.bestFor: Small living rooms and balconies that want a light concrete-look drum.

28 in diameter fits small rooms and corners easily
Lighter than real concrete, so it is easy to reposition

products.name: Christopher Knight Home Patsy Lightweight Concrete MgO Round Coffee Table, Indoor and Outdoor

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Coffee or side table, indoor and outdoor

products.description:
The Patsy is a lightweight concrete round-top table made of MGO material that the listing says blends clean lines with the resilience needed outdoors and can serve as a coffee or accent table. The listing stresses a minimalist profile and adaptable dimensions. It is the most flexible table in the lineup in terms of use.

The tradeoff is documentation. The text we reviewed gives no diameter, height or weight, so you must check the listing page for the exact size. MGO is a mineral board that resists moisture but can chip, and a lightweight table can slide or tip if bumped. Compared with the FESTIVITY, it is similar in material but less specific.

Confirm the dimensions before ordering and seal the surface if you place it outdoors. It suits a living room or a patio where one light table has to move between roles.

products.name: CIMOTA 44 in Lightweight Concrete Round Coffee Table with Pedestal Base, Distressed Finish
products.description:
The CIMOTA is a 44 in round coffee table made of lightweight concrete on a stable pedestal base with a handcrafted, weathered, textured distressed finish. The listing says the large circular surface holds a lot. It is the largest table in the lineup.

The tradeoff is size and finish. A 44 in round table needs a generous room, and a distressed finish hides some marks but is a strong look that may not suit a clean modern space. A pedestal base gives knee room but concentrates the weight under the center, and the listing does not state weight. Compared with the Modway, it is larger and lighter but less polished.

Use a felt pad under the base and check the stability on arrival. It suits a large living room with a sectional where a big round centerpiece is wanted.

products.name: homary Round Concrete Coffee Table, Desert Sand Cement Top, Walnut Ash Wood Legs
products.description:
The homary is a round coffee table with a natural cement top in a desert sand finish on solid ash wood legs in a walnut tone, with smooth, rounded edges and a sculptural base. The listing describes it as a Japandi piece. It is the only table here that combines a cement top with solid wood legs.

The tradeoff is the contrast of materials. A cement top is heavy and can stress thin legs, so check that the legs are bolted firmly, and cement is porous, so an unsealed top can stain. The listing text does not give the diameter or height, so check the page. Compared with the Modway, it is warmer in look and less monolithic.

Tighten the leg bolts after the first month and wipe spills quickly. It suits a Japandi or Scandinavian living room where a warm wood and a pale cement top are the point.

cons: Listing text gives no diameter or height

products.name: MaiDeHaoo 43 in Oval Faux Stone Coffee Table, Single-Mold Fiberglass, Irregular Shape
products.description:
The MaiDeHaoo is a 43 in oval faux stone coffee table made of single-mold fiberglass with a matte finish, an irregular shape and rounded edges. The listing says it is stable and comfortable. It is the only table here that is not concrete or board but fiberglass that imitates stone.

The tradeoff is honesty about material. Fiberglass is light and strong but is plastic-based, so it will not feel or age like concrete, and a scratch cannot be sanded out like stone. A single-mold build has no seams, which helps. Compared with the CIMOTA, it is lighter and seamless but a different material.

Wipe it with a damp cloth and avoid abrasive cleaners that dull the matte finish. It suits a living room where a light, seamless, organic table is wanted and real concrete is not.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Poured concrete is heavy and porous. Lightweight concrete, MgO board and fiberglass are lighter and cheaper but behave differently. The Modway and homary say concrete or cement, the Patsy and CIMOTA say lightweight concrete, the FESTIVITY says MgO and the MaiDeHaoo says fiberglass. Read the material line before the name. A listing that uses the word concrete in the title but describes MgO or fiberglass in the bullets is telling you the real material, and the bullets are the part to trust.

Standard concrete tables weigh roughly 80 to 150 lb, and fiber-reinforced ones are lighter. A heavy table is stable but hard to move and can stress an upper-floor apartment. Hollow or MgO tables are light. Check the weight on the listing page, and ask whether the floor can carry it if you live above ground level. A very heavy table on a small footprint concentrates load, and a spread base or a pad helps.

Concrete and cement absorb liquids, so oil, wine and coffee can stain an unsealed top. A penetrating sealer helps and needs renewing every year or two. MgO resists water better but is also porous on the surface. Use coasters and wipe spills. A sealed surface still stains if a spill sits overnight, so treat a ring of wine like a ring on wood and wipe it before it dries.

The Modway, CIMOTA, Patsy and FESTIVITY all mention outdoor use. Freeze and thaw can crack porous materials, so cover outdoor tables in winter. Sun can fade pigmented finishes. Choose a covered patio over an open one, and bring a light table indoors in a storm, since a gust can tip an empty MgO drum more easily than you expect.

A drum, like the Modway or FESTIVITY, is solid and has no leg room. A pedestal, as on the CIMOTA, gives knee room. Legged tables like the homary are lighter on the floor. Round shapes suit tight rooms and avoid sharp corners. If a table is as wide as your sofa is deep, leave extra room in the walkway.

A heavy concrete base can scratch hardwood and crack tile if dropped. Felt or rubber pads protect floors and reduce sliding. Check that the base is flat. A chipped edge on a drum can scratch a floor too, so check the base rim for chips on arrival and sand or fill them before placing the table.

howWeEvaluated.title: Listing specifications
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each table from the material, dimensions, finish and use stated on its Amazon listing. We did not handle any of them. The Modway's 34 in diameter and the CIMOTA's 44 in diameter are numbers we compare.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We recorded what each table is really made of, because concrete, MgO and fiberglass are very different. Where a listing was vague, we say so. That is why the Modway ranks first.

howWeEvaluated.title: On-topic filtering
howWeEvaluated.description: The topic search returned lift-top tables, faux marble tables and a nesting set. We kept tables with a concrete or concrete-look claim. That left a lineup of six.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered recurring themes such as staining, chipped rims and heavy deliveries. We do not repeat ratings or counts. A pattern counted only when it matched the described construction.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest limits
howWeEvaluated.description: Several listings give no weight or dimensions in the text we reviewed. We say so plainly. Treat weights as unknown until you check the listing page.

cards.label: Concrete or cement
cards.text: The Modway and homary are heavy, solid and porous. They age well with sealing and are hard to move.

cards.label: Concrete-look
cards.text: The FESTIVITY, Patsy and MaiDeHaoo are light, easy to move and cheaper. They chip or scratch in different ways.

howToChoose.note: Choose real concrete for a lasting, heavy centerpiece and a light look-alike for flexibility.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A moisture-resistant material, a sealed top, a base that will not rust and a cover for winter. Avoid unsealed porous tops in freezing climates.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Modway, CIMOTA, Patsy and FESTIVITY all mention outdoor use, with the MgO tables handling moisture best.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a poured concrete top with a stated weight, a sealed finish and a repairable surface. Those sit above these listings.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want the look in a small room. A light drum like the FESTIVITY covers that.

maintenance.why: Sealer wears off and liquids soak in. Reseal the Modway and homary tops.
Oil and wine stain porous surfaces. Blot and wipe with mild soap.
Heat and water mark concrete, and bases scratch floors. Protect the surface and the floor.
MgO and fiberglass chip at the rim. Touch up or fill small chips early.
Freeze and thaw cracks porous materials. Cover the CIMOTA and Patsy outdoors.

faq.q: Is a concrete coffee table heavy?
faq.a: Real concrete often weighs 80 to 150 lb. Lightweight and MgO tables are much lighter.
Unsealed concrete can stain from oil, wine and coffee. A sealer helps and needs renewing.

faq.q: Can I use a concrete table outdoors?
faq.a: Several listings say so, but freeze and thaw can crack porous materials. Cover it in winter.

faq.q: Is MgO the same as concrete?
faq.a: No. It is a mineral board that resists moisture and looks like concrete. It can chip at edges.

faq.q: Will a concrete table scratch my floor?
faq.a: It can, because it is heavy and hard. Use felt or rubber pads.
It is light and seamless, but plastic-based. It will not age like stone and scratches cannot be sanded out.
